title: Risk-thread notes — SOC2 prep (scratch)
content:
Quick brain dump while mapping controls to actual product touchpoints — messy. Intended to be a running diary of open questions, small experiments, and what I need to hand off to ENG/SRE/Product later.

Context and goal:
- Prep for SOC2 readiness review (targeting initial readiness check in April).
- Focus: evidence collection for A.1 (access control), A.3 (change management), and A.5 (monitoring/logging) — mapping existing artifacts to common control statements.
- Keep notes about how Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments differ for evidence (esp. on private where customer-managed KMS comes in).

Things I observed (raw):
- Access control: console uses Okta SSO; service-to-service auth uses mTLS and signed tokens. Need explicit docs for service token rotation frequency and how we revoke (is it in infra-runbook?). Ticket: INF-2345 references token rotation work but not runbook.
- KMS: Hosted uses Redwood KMS (AWS KMS CMKs). Private offering points to customer KMS; evidence trail inconsistent across private installs. Ask PS: what artifacts do we get from on-prem install? (audit logs, KMS policy snapshots).
- Logs: central ELK cluster for hosted, but Dedicated customers may have separate logging sinks; need a matrix of where logs live per deployment type.

Open questions (prioritized):
1) Evidence for user access reviews: who signs off, cadence? Product says quarterly but can't find signed review artifacts for last two quarters. Who owns exec signoff? (ping Lena)
2) Change control: PR approvals exist but change window approvals for infra changes (cluster upgrades) are not consistently captured. Is there a single ticket tag we can query? Maybe use label "maintenance-window" — check with release-eng.
3) Incident response timelines: we have PagerDuty playbooks, but the post-incident review (PIR) template isn't standardized. Need a minimal PIR template for SOC2 evidence.

Quick mapping sketch (control -> artifact examples):
- Logical access: Okta audit export (CSV), identity provider config screenshots, HR termination sync logs (workday -> Okta sync).
- Provisioning/deprovisioning: GitHub org membership change logs, jira tickets for access requests (JIRA-SEC-90), ad-hoc slack approvals — need to capture those in a ticketed workflow or copy of message archived.
- Change management: PR + changelog + deployment runbook (deploy traces from CI). For major infra changes: meeting minutes (release notes) + rollback plan.
- Monitoring: CloudWatch alarms + pager logs + SLI dashboards (console path: Console -> Observability -> Per-route dashboards). Take screenshots with timestamps.

Small checklist (things I can do now):
- [ ] Export Okta org logs for Oct 2025–Mar 2026 (request via SC-ops).
- [ ] Pull list of KMS keys in Hosted account and attach key policy snapshots.
- [ ] Create a minimal PIR template and share in #trust-ops for feedback.
- [ ] Draft a short one-pager on how Private deployments differ for auditors (3 bullets).
- [ ] Tag PRs that included infra changes with "infra-change" and create a saved filter in GitHub.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- For auditors, snapshots/screenshots with timestamps + export files are usually accepted. Keep raw exports though (CSV/JSON) not just screenshots.
- When in doubt, capture both: short explanatory note + primary evidence.
- Lean on PS for private-deploy evidence — they have install checklists but not retained in central repo. Ask to start copying artifact manifest to shared s3.

Potential risks / escalations:
- Private deployments: gaps in centralized evidence (risk: inability to show uniform control implementation). Mitigation: require a minimal evidence kit as part of every private deploy.
- Service tokens: unclear rotation/revocation process — medium risk for access control.
- Audit trail retention: logs are kept for 90 days in some envs; SOC2 reviewers might expect 12 months for certain records. Need policy alignment.

Random fragments / links to stitch into final doc:
- "confluence: CON-SEC-1122" (policy draft for logical access)
- "jira: JIRA-SEC-90" (access review request)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1024 (infra change with deploy notes)
- slack convo (trust-ops #) TS=1679900000 — save permalink

Who to loop in next: Lena (access reviews), Ramon (dedicated/private onboarding evidence), Jaime from release-eng (change window tagging), PS lead (for private installs).

Draft paragraph for auditors (very rough):
"Redwood enforces role-based access through SSO (Okta) and automated provisioning linked to HR. All infrastructure changes are executed through our CI/CD pipeline with PR approvals and documented runbooks; major changes use scheduled maintenance windows and rollback plans. For Private deployments, a standardized evidence kit is produced during on-boarding to demonstrate parity of controls despite customer-managed infrastructure."

Final notes: keep this file informal. I'll convert to a formal control mapping table next sprint. Save TODOs and open Qs as tickets so we don't lose them in Slack.
